note: Arguments for survivors that no test can kill, keyed by mutant name (the part after the last dot). Read by scripts/check_survivors.py --finalize. Each reason is one sentence and is an argument from reading the code, checked only in that the final test selection (and, where listed in the triage file, the slow tests) does not distinguish the mutant.

rules.reason: The argsort tie order only decides which of two pieces is called A and which B, D changes sign, and everything later (squared norm, magnitudes, pair key) is symmetric, so the results are bitwise identical.
np.searchsorted defaults to side='left'.
cap * cap is infinite for an infinite cap, and for a NaN cap both versions skip the pruning because nan < inf is false.
When e <= i + 1 the slice (i + 1, e) is empty, so skipping it or not selects nothing either way.
einsum subscript letters are labels, so 'IJ,IJ->I' is the same contraction as 'ij,ij->i'.
The filled index array gets the default integer dtype, which indexes just as well as int64.
rs is only used inside the vertex value, which is selected only where p2 > 0, so its value for p2 <= 0 is never read.
For p2 == 0 the vertex value becomes p1 * 0 + 0 = 0, which is never below the end-point candidate min(p1 w, -p1 w) <= 0, so the minimum is unchanged.
For K = 1 the slice nrm[:, 1:] is empty, so the sum is zero with or without the guard.
For K <= 2 the product has at most three columns, so P[:, 3:] is empty and the tail sum is zero with or without the guard.

The replaced default applies only to non-finite pieces, which _pieces builds as constants (every coefficient above the constant term is zero), so midpoint, half-width, shift and magnitude point cannot change the box.
Integer coefficient arrays are widened to float wherever they are used (hold values come from a float accumulator and cf is a float array), and np.isfinite accepts integers.
For i >= K - 1 the inner range(K - 2, i - 1, -1) is empty, so extra outer iterations do nothing.
The start of an overlap that is not finite is masked out by the later np.where(fin, ..., 0) in xa, xb and h and is read nowhere else.
The replaced default applies only to head-head and tail-tail pairs, whose pieces are constants, so a different time offset changes neither D nor the magnitudes.
A wider slice only recomputes chunks that are already computed, with identical values, and np.minimum.at is idempotent.

Step 1 instead of the chunk size only recomputes overlapping chunks with identical values (results equal); it is caught only by the runtime bound of the slow test_hundred_drone_fleet_is_fast, a performance kill and not a change of any result.
The lower bound is already at most min(u - tol, cap) <= u.min(), because a sound cell bound cannot exceed the witness of the cell that produced u, so the clamp to u.min() only guards rounding.
int(kq / nd) truncates to the same drone index as kq // nd for every key below 2**53 and fleet below 2**26 drones.
A float flag array behaves as the boolean one: True is stored as 1.0 and tested by truthiness.
done only triggers an early exit; without it the remaining candidates are all skipped because every drone already has a target.
scipy cdist uses the euclidean metric by default and accepts the metric name in any case.
Generator.choice treats replace=None as falsy, which is the value replace=False the code passes.
block only sets the row-block size; the count is the same for every block size.
The division is by np.where(a > 1e-18, a, 1.0), which is never zero, so ignoring or reporting 'divide' changes nothing.

At a == 1e-18 exactly the closest-approach parameter changes from 0 to -b, and since b^2 <= c a = 1e-18 c the squared distance c + 2 b u + a u^2 differs from c by less than half an ulp of c, so it is bitwise the same.
The inner divisor is only used where the outer test a > 1e-18 holds, where the strict and the non-strict inner test agree.
The fallback divisor is only used where the outer test fails, and those lanes are discarded by the outer np.where.
